title: Find the weaknesses in a bedside note
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.
The exercise has not been tested with learners, and its Arabic version has not been written.
The Open RN text is US-oriented; legal wording and retention rules differ by jurisdiction.
Whether an abbreviation is acceptable is a local list decision.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
objectives: Recognise features that make a record unsafe to rely on.

sources.use: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals 2.5: documentation principles and error correction

required_sources: The employer's documentation policy and approved abbreviation list
A national professional standard on record keeping for the jurisdiction
setup: A fictional bedside note written by a fictional nurse.
prompt: Select the lines that weaken the record.

lines.text: 14:20 Told Dr Lee by phone that the patient has a new cough; asked for review; Dr Lee will see the patient by 15:00. A. Nurse, RN, 12 March.
lines.why: Dated, timed, signed, factual, says who was told and what happens next.

lines.text: The patient was uncooperative and difficult.
lines.why: Documentation should be objective, factual and professional; describe what was seen and said.
Abbreviations should be avoided in legal documentation.
Do not document in advance of completing a task.
Only recording that something was done tells the next reader nothing; record the findings.

lines.text: (an entry with no time and no signature)
lines.why: All documentation must include date, time and signature.
